definitions.explanation: Describes someone who can wait calmly and does not get annoyed when things take a long time. Literally 'one's temperament is long.' The direct antonym of {気|き}が{短|みじか}い.

examples.japanese: {気|き}が{長|なが}い{人|ひと}が{子|こ}どもの{相手|あいて}に{向|む}いている。
examples.english: Patient people are suited to dealing with children.

examples.japanese: {十年|じゅうねん}かけて{研究|けんきゅう}を{続|つづ}けるとは、ずいぶん{気|き}が{長|なが}い{話|はなし}だ。
examples.english: Continuing the research for ten years — that's quite a long-haul undertaking.

examples.japanese: {祖父|そふ}は{気|き}が{長|なが}くて、{何時間|なんじかん}{待|ま}たされても{文句|もんく}を{言|い}わない。
examples.english: My grandfather is even-tempered and doesn't complain no matter how many hours he's kept waiting.

notes:
STRUCTURE: {気|き} (temperament) + が + {長|なが}い (long).

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {気|き}が{長|なが}い{人|ひと}: a patient person
- {気|き}{長|なが}に{待|ま}つ: to wait patiently (the adverbial form {気|き}{長|なが}に is very common)
- {気|き}が{長|なが}い{話|はなし}: a long-drawn-out proposition

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {我慢強|がまんづよ}い: patient, enduring — stresses putting up with hardship, not just waiting calmly
- のんびり: laid-back — describes an unhurried pace of life rather than tolerance of delay

USAGE:
Applied to a plan rather than a person, {気|き}が{長|なが}い suggests the speaker finds it impractically slow.
